projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained count of 16-18 'mobile' devices combined with zero camera motion during a weekday morning strongly suggests IoT devices (tablets, smart displays, or laptops) are being misclassified as phones, or multiple guests are present; this matters because it may skew occupancy-based automations or mask true home status.

The sustained count of 16-21 connected devices far exceeds the expected 4-8 for a family of four, and combined with zero morning camera activity, strongly indicates either unannounced guests staying out of view or a network/IoT device reporting anomaly that warrants verification.

The sustained count of 17-20 mobile devices over the last hour, paired with zero camera activity on a Wednesday morning, strongly suggests a presence detection anomaly or stale network connections rather than actual occupancy. This discrepancy warrants verification to rule out a network glitch or ensure the system isn't masking a false sense of presence.

The steady decline in connected devices from 07:59 to 08:15 (21 to 19), paired with zero camera motion and the Wednesday morning timeframe, indicates the household is likely in the process of leaving for school and work. This normal departure pattern explains the earlier high device count as likely overnight network artifacts or standby devices.

The high, rapidly fluctuating device count (23–26) during early morning hours, combined with zero camera activity, indicates the network is counting dormant IoT devices and wearables cycling Wi-Fi/Bluetooth sleep modes rather than active human presence. This explains the fluctuations and suggests normal overnight network behavior rather than a security concern.

Between 3:55 AM and 5:10 AM, the network reports 24–26 mobile devices connected, fluctuating rapidly, which is highly abnormal for a household of four and suggests either network instability, miscounted IoT devices, or unauthorized access during sleeping hours. This warrants a quick network check to rule out security issues or connectivity problems.

Cross-referencing the stable 25-27 device count with zero camera motion and confirmed sleep data confirms the household is securely asleep; the high device count is a normal smart home baseline rather than an active presence or network anomaly.

The stable 25-27 device count paired with zero camera motion at 10:56 PM confirms the household is in a settled, low-activity state; the high count reflects the family's normal IoT/mobile baseline rather than active presence, and the recurring pattern indicates this is expected evening operation, not a security concern.

The sustained 22-26 device count paired with zero camera motion late at night strongly suggests unsegmented IoT devices are being counted as mobile clients, but it still warrants a quick network audit to rule out unauthorized access or neighbor piggybacking.

The sustained count of 22-24 connected mobile devices paired with zero camera motion over a four-hour Tuesday evening window strongly suggests either a network/IoT device misclassification or that the household is actually empty. This discrepancy warrants verification to rule out a false presence alert or an unreported absence.
